title: model-metadata: add schema_v1 structs + validation for model/version records
author: Quentin Harris
release_notes: Internal-only: introduces schema_v1 types + validation helpers for model/version metadata; no API surface changes yet (behind feature flag in service layer).
description: Summary: This PR introduces schema_v1 structs for ModelRecord + VersionRecord and implements baseline validation rules to support the v1 Model Metadata Schema workstream. It also adds unit tests and scaffolding for the upcoming migration/backfill tooling. Motivation: We need a canonical, versioned schema with consistent validation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so that downstream change-event emission and customer-facing changelog generation can rely on well-formed metadata. Today the registry accepts a mix of fields with inconsistent defaults and insufficient constraints (e.g., version_id formatting, context length bounds, incompatible capability flags). What’s included: (1) New schema_v1 package with typed structs (ModelRecordV1, ModelVersionV1, CapabilityFlagsV1, ProvenanceV1, CompatibilityV1, QuantizationProfileV1). (2) Validation rules + error codes with deterministic output for callers (ValidateModelRecordV1, ValidateModelVersionV1). (3) Feature-gated wiring in service layer to validate on create/update for v1 payloads (existing v0 code path unchanged). (4) Unit tests for required/optional fields, naming conventions, and a set of fixture examples. (5) Migration scaffolding: basic adapters for reading existing DB rows into v1 structs and emitting a “needs_backfill” report (no writes in this PR). Validation rules (initial set): - model_id must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,62}$ and be stable across deployments - version_id must match ^v\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(-[a-z0-9]+)?$ (date-based) - display_name required, <= 64 chars; description <= 280 chars - context_window_tokens must be in [1024, 1048576] - capabilities: tool_calling and structured_output require chat=true; embeddings=true cannot be combined with chat=true for the same version record (separate SKU) - quantization: if quantized=true then quantization.bits must be one of {4, 8} and quantization.method required - compatibility matrix: at least one deployment_mode in {hosted, dedicated, private}; private requires a non-empty “supported_runtimes” list - provenance.source must be in {"upstream_open", "upstream_commercial", "redwood_finetune", "redwood_distill"}; if upstream_* then upstream_repo/upstream_model_name required - deprecation fields intentionally not included yet in v1 structs (tracked in ENG-4921 follow-up; see Open questions) Testing: Adds ~40 unit tests for schema_v1 validation plus fixtures for a handful of common catalog entries. Tests are deterministic and snapshot-like (stringified errors sorted by field path). Open questions / follow-ups: - Deprecation/sunset fields will land in a separate PR once Product signs off on customer-visible messaging constraints (ENG-4921). - Confirm whether version_id should allow semantic versions for vendor models that don’t release by date; current stance is date-based for Redwood-served versions. - Decide whether to allow a combined “chat+embeddings” version record for certain multi-head models; current validation rejects to keep routing and pricing unambiguous. Rollout plan: Land structs + validation first (this PR). Next, migrate existing records behind an offline backfill job (ENG-4924) and then switch service default writes to v1 after we have coverage for top catalog models and a safe rollback plan.
commits: model-registry: add schema_v1 types for model + version metadata
validation: implement ValidateModelRecordV1 / ValidateModelVersionV1 with stable error codes
service: feature-gate v1 validation on write paths
tests: add fixtures + unit tests for v1 validation rules
migrations: add v1 adapter scaffolding + backfill report command
review_conversation: Michael Nguyen: The structs look good. Two questions: (1) can we standardize error paths to be JSON-pointer-ish? (2) version_id regex is strict—will we regret this for upstream vendor versions? Also, please add at least one test covering tool_calling => chat requirement.

Quentin Harris (author): (1) Good call. I updated error paths to use dot notation consistently (e.g., "compatibility.deployment_modes") and ensured deterministic sorting; JSON pointer could be follow-up but I’d rather not churn call sites now. (2) Agreed it’s strict; current goal is to make Redwood-served versions predictable for changelog + pinning. I added an open question + linked it to ENG-4922 notes. Added tool_calling/chat test in latest push.
Chloe Martin: On compatibility: private requires supported_runtimes list—can we make that optional until Private team confirms the field list? I’m worried this blocks migration.

Quentin Harris (author): I made it required only when deployment_modes includes private. For migration scaffolding, the backfill report will flag missing supported_runtimes but doesn’t write/validate in the v0 path, so we can backfill incrementally without breaking existing reads.

Jordan Lee: Please ensure we’re not mixing internal-only fields here. Can you add a comment / guardrail that these are internal structs and not the customer-safe allowlist? Also +1 to stable error codes.

Quentin Harris (author): Added module-level docstring clarifying these structs include internal metadata and are not directly publishable; public allowlist/redaction is tracked in a later PR in the changelog generator pipeline. Error codes are now constants and covered in tests.
Jada Williams: Minor: capability validation message should be customer-safe since it may bubble to operators. Replace "SKU" wording. Also can we return multiple errors (not fail-fast)?
Quentin Harris (author): Updated message text to be neutral ("unsupported combination") and validation now aggregates all errors before returning.
final_review: Michael Nguyen: Approved (with note to revisit version_id flexibility before GA).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Quentin Harris on 2026-01-20. Squash commit: 8c3e9d1 model-metadata: schema_v1 structs + validation.
